title: An early safety detail that stays relevant after many notes
description: A drug allergy and the place of a spare key are written once at the start, followed by thirty ordinary notes. Nothing changes; the early facts must still be found.

notes.text: Mum is allergic to penicillin. Remind any new doctor or pharmacist.
The spare front door key is under the green flowerpot by the shed.
Bought bread, milk and bananas.
Rain all day. Stayed in and tidied the spare room.
Called the council about the missed bin collection.
Watched a documentary about bees.
Book club meets next Thursday.
Fixed the squeaky door in the hall.
Made lentil soup. There is plenty left.
Washed the car and hoovered inside.
Posted the birthday card to Auntie Jean.
Cut the hedge at the front.
Library book due back on Friday.
Ran out of printer ink. Order more.
Neighbours' dog was barking again last night.
Walked to the canal and back, about an hour.
Changed the bed sheets.
Took the old microwave to the tip.
Planted tomato seedlings on the windowsill.
Phone bill came. Nothing unusual.
Sorted the recycling.
Watered the geraniums.
Lunch with Rita at the cafe on the high street.
Ordered new curtains for the living room.
Defrosted the freezer.
Heard a woodpecker in the garden this morning.
Bought stamps and envelopes.
Quiz night at the pub was fun; we came third.
Charged the tablet and updated the apps.
Cleaned the oven.
Collected a parcel from the post office.
Watched the football with Dad.

questions.why: Written in the first note, asked after thirty others.

questions.ask: Where is the spare front door key?
questions.why: Written in note 2, asked after thirty others.

questions.why: Two old facts in one answer.
